result:
Make it so that no human being could inflict suffering on another without immediately and viscerally feeling the exact physical and emotional weight of that suffering themselves.

Almost every systemic catastrophe—war, exploitation, cruelty, neglect—relies on distance. It relies on the ability of decision-makers to insulate themselves from the consequences of their choices, or on people dehumanizing others so they don't have to feel what they are doing.

If empathy were not an optional moral virtue, but an unavoidable sensory reality, self-interest and the collective good would instantly become the exact same thing. You wouldn't need to convince people to be kind or legislate against cruelty; the basic architecture of human experience would make harming someone else feel identical to harming yourself.
